patch:
diff --git a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
index 55fa844..732136e 100644
--- a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
+++ b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
@@ -1,11 +1,10 @@
-from store import CUSTOMERS, ORDERS
+from store import ORDERS
 
 
 def orders_for_customer(customer):
     """All orders belonging to `customer`."""
     rows = []
     for order in ORDERS:
-        owner = next(c for c in CUSTOMERS if c["id"] == order["customer_id"])
-        if owner["name"] == customer["name"]:
+        if order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]:
             rows.append(order)
     return rows
verification: 1) Baseline run_tests.py -> 'visible tests passed'. 2) Baseline report dump showed 6 lines with cross-customer leakage and 101/102 duplicated; total 290. 3) Applied fix. 4) Post-fix run_tests.py -> passed. 5) Post-fix report: exactly 4 correct lines, total 165. 6) Integrity assertions ran clean: no duplicate order_ids; every (email,order_id) pair maps to the order's true customer_id -> 'OK: no duplicate lines; every order shown to its true owner'. 7) git status --short shows only queries.py modified.
cause: orders_for_customer matched an order to a customer by name rather than the unique id; two distinct customers share the name 'Acme', so each Acme order matched both, leaking across statements and duplicating report lines. Matching on order["customer_id"] == customer["id"] ties each order to its single true owner; Zenith's genuinely distinct 103/104 remain.
